thread:
Ava Chen: heads-up — OmniHealth go-live tomorrow 9am PT. they want best-effort low-latency for search/autocomplete and are flagged as renewal-risk (trial upsell). need a concise prefill + streaming fallback runbook.
Ravi Patel: ack. do they expect steady traffic or spikes initially?
Ava Chen: estimator from sales says 50 qps steady, spikes to 300 qps first hour. sensitive PII, so no external caching. we can use tenant-scoped prefill and per-req KV cache.
Marta Lopez: ok — tenant-scoped warm pools make sense. suggest: 1) prefill top-50 prefixes into in-memory cache, 2) enable short TTL (3m) and sliding refresh on hits, 3) enable streaming fallback to non-prefill when miss >200ms.
Liam O'Neill: can we do controlled warmup to avoid cost blast? maybe staged ramp and canary by reps.
Ravi Patel: implementation notes:
- warm pool pods: x4 gpus dedicated for their tenant during t0 (first 2 hours)
- batching window: 5-10ms for steady traffic, auto-disable if latency >150ms
- prefill job: run 5min before go-live, async prefill endpoint: POST /admin/prefill {"tenant":"omni","keys":[]}
Marta Lopez: sample prefill curl (ops):
```
curl -X POST https://console.api.redwood/prefill \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tenant":"omni","prefixes":["patient:","record:","rx:"]}'
```
Ava Chen: @ravi can you add a step in runbook to tag cache entries with `no-export` and to mandate encryption at rest? legal requires KMS logs.
Ravi Patel: yes — policy: tenant-cache-meta {"export":false,"kms":"redwood-kms-01"}. i'll add enforcement in the prefill lambda.
Liam O'Neill: for the renewal signal — capture 3 metrics we can share with CSMs in realtime: 1) 99p latency for tenant, 2) percent prefills hit, 3) cost delta vs baseline. send to /cs/telemetry channel.
Marta Lopez: telemetry event example (json):
```
{ "tenant":"omni", "time":"{{ts}}", "prefill_hit_pct":72, "p99_ms":88, "cost_per_1k":0.42 }
```
Ava Chen: great. also add a recovery plan if warm pool OOMs: fallback to smaller quantized model + reduced batch size + notify CS.
Ravi Patel: fallback policy implemented:
- immediate switch to q4_0_small variant
- reduce batch-size to 1
- enable streaming-only path to preserve throughput
- create incident: /inc/auto (deploy-bot will post)
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-6147 — "omni warmpool OOM" (assigned to eng-oncall)
Marta Lopez: rollout plan for tomorrow:
1) prefill run (5min prior)
2) enable warm pool (canary on 1% of traffic for 10m)
3) monitor telemetry (p99, prefill_hit, cpu/gpu mem)
4) ramp to 10%/50%/100% over 30min if stable
Ava Chen: CS checklist for handoff:
- verify user tokens provisioned
- confirm KMS keys in place
- confirm prefill run outputs >60% hit for top-50 prefixes
- set renewal watch flag if hit_pct < 40 after 60m
Ravi Patel: command to run quick prefill dry-run:
```
POST /admin/prefill/dryrun {"tenant":"omni","sample_size":200}
```
Response will return expected hit distribution.
Liam O'Neill: post-mortem criteria: if cost >2x predicted or p99 >250ms for >15m then pause and rollback to baseline model.
Ava Chen: thanks team — i'll add these steps to the customer-facing runbook doc and share with OmniHealth for approval. please review before 6pm PT.
Marta Lopez: reviewed. added a note about short-term quotas to avoid runaway billing.
Ravi Patel: added enforcement for `no-export` and the dry-run endpoint. pushing config now.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: prefill-lambda v2.3.1 at 1769543330 :rocket:
Ava Chen: perfect — i'll DM sales and cs leads, and schedule a 8:30am quick sync 30min before go-live. :thumbsup:
